subject: FY2023 Budget and Municipal Funding Reallocations
overview: The City Council approved the $201 million fiscal year 2023 budget after a six-hour session involving intense negotiations with the Mayor and significant testimony from educators and municipal staff. The final agreement included reallocating funds to support library operations, school positions, and dedicated legal counsel for the Council.

items.title: Year-End Transfers for FY2022 (Paper 22-422)
items.summary: The Council approved $708,877 in year-end transfers, though a $55,000 transfer to the law department was initially contested due to concerns over undisclosed legal settlements and lack of transparency.

items.title: Use of Retained Earnings for Water and Sewer (Paper 22-423)
items.summary: Approved the appropriation of $500,000 from retained earnings to subsidize the Water and Sewer Enterprise Fund for FY2023 to mitigate rate increases.

items.title: Casino Community Impact Funds Appropriation (Paper 22-424)
items.summary: Approved $135,247 in casino funds to hire a transportation engineer and a motor vehicle repairman in the DPW as per the surrounding community agreement.

items.title: Cemetery Perpetual Care and Salary Appropriations (Papers 22-425, 22-427)
items.summary: Approved routine annual appropriations from cemetery perpetual care and grave sale funds for cemetery operations and salaries.

items.title: Appropriations for Police Cruisers and DPW Equipment (Paper 22-426)
items.summary: Approved $305,000 from free cash for three hybrid police cruisers, a groundwater remediation project, and recreation lease payments, alongside $220,000 from water enterprise earnings for DPW trucks.

items.title: ARPA Revenue Loss Allocation (Paper 22-428)
items.summary: Approved $7,292,100 in ARPA funds to cover revenue shortfalls and fund personnel salaries in the school, fire, police, and DPW departments.

items.title: FY2023 Revised Budget Submission (Paper 22-408)
items.summary: Following nearly five hours of debate and public testimony from teachers and staff regarding level funding during high inflation, the Council negotiated a deal to pass the budget as amended. The final agreement reallocated $240,000 from facilities maintenance to fund library salaries, an assistant city solicitor, elections, and council consultants, while using $300,000 in ARPA funds to restore educator positions.

items.title: Grant of Location: Harvard Street Gas Regulator (Paper 22-409)
items.summary: Approved a petition by National Grid to install a replacement regulator station in the Harvard Street sidewalk following technical review and neighbor notification conditions.

items.title: CPC Appropriation: Thomas Brooks Park Restoration (Paper 22-429)
items.summary: Approved $65,500 from Community Preservation Act reserves for phase one of the Thomas Brooks Park master plan, specifically for stone wall restoration.

items.title: CPC Appointment and Meeting Records
items.summary: The Council confirmed the appointment of Matthew Leming to the Community Preservation Committee and approved meeting records from June 21 and June 22, 2022.
